Scope: infrastructure networks over about 3.5 km² in Zones A and B and the Labour Community Area, around 100 km south-east of Riyadh.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. Against the revised plan issued on 26 Oct, the project is 0.09% ahead: 51.79% complete against 51.70% planned. The lead is down from 0.24% last week, because this week's gain of 0.75% fell short of the 0.89% planned, and construction itself is now 0.2% behind its plan.

The P6 finish is back on the contract date, but every interim milestone slipped another 5 to 7 days. The P6 update uploaded this week (data date 17-Nov-2026) finishes the project on 02-Dec-2027 with zero float, a week earlier than last week, while road works moved to 14-Jan-2027 and the MV network to 20-Feb-2027, 104 and 141 days after their baseline dates. Open activities with negative float rose from 610 to 638. Weekly progress was below plan for the second week running, and asphalt works still face a bitumen supply constraint. Against the original baseline, which called for 87.1% by the end of November, the project remains far behind.

Interim milestones slipped 5 to 7 days while the project finish moved a week earlier. With the data date one week later, every open interim milestone moved 5 to 7 days and lost 5 to 6 days of float, so the driving work again barely advanced. The project finish, however, moved from 09-Dec-2027 back to 02-Dec-2027 with zero float, and 56 open activities still finish after it, up to 09-Oct-2028. Open activities with negative float rose from 610 to 638, led by bituminous construction (20) and aggregate base course (19). The worst float, −121 days, sits on the asphalt binder, aggregate base course and MV trenching. P6 finishes the telecom network on 09-Jun-2027, more than two months after the weekly report's "All networks" forecast of 05-Apr-2027.

Data notes

  • The P6 project finish moved from 09-Dec-2027 back to 02-Dec-2027 with zero float, although every open interim milestone slipped 5 to 7 days and lost float, and 56 open activities (mainly curbstone, short-lead civil items, mosque superstructure and GRP pipes) still finish after it, up to 09-Oct-2028. The update does not explain the change; it may come from a constraint or a logic change rather than recovered work.
  • The weekly report's milestone forecasts (road works 09-Jan-2027, MV network 15-Feb-2027) did not move, while the P6 update gives 14-Jan-2027 and 20-Feb-2027. The main summary sheet again shows the milestone forecasts as the baseline dates.
  • The major quantity tracker shows exactly the same totals as last week for all four items, although the FIR log lists aggregate base course, subgrade and prime coat inspections this week. The 15-Nov progress presentation again has its network layouts and material progress sheet as images only.
  • Quality: the weekly quality sheet counts 193 FIRs (box culvert 13, sewer 36, storm 36), but the FIR summary lists 203 (box culvert 28, sewer 39, storm 28); the box culvert row is identical to last week's and the sewer and storm rows are identical to each other. Cumulative NCRs read 45 against 42 last week while 0 are shown as issued this week. The period is again written "08-November-2026 to 14-October-2026". The Quality-Stat sheet reports cost-based progress as "actual"; it is not used here.
  • Invoice Log: unchanged; invoices 1–5 remain entered at their after-retention values with retention 0, so the 58,434,344 "gross" total is after retention for those invoices. The summary still counts 0 submitted invoices. The FIR value to date fell from 67,676,799 to 66,732,799.
  • Procurement: MV cable, lighting poles, sluice valves and GRP pipes still show a delivery completion date of 20-Oct although they are incomplete. Interlock deliveries rose again although supply is recorded as on hold. One row (970 of 1,152 nos) has no material name and is not shown.
  • The photo titles in the Weekly Progress Photos sheet ("Concrete barriers delivery", "Temporary mobilization Area", "Start works in Area A") are the same as last week and do not match the new photos, which have no date or GPS stamp.
